{{recipe}}

A recipe from Nova Scotia that is called both '''Scottish bannock''' and '''Irish soda bread'''.

==Ingredients==
* 4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (950 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[cookbook:Flour|whole wheat flour]]
* ½ cup (120 ml) white granulated [[cookbook:sugar|sugar]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Baking Soda|baking soda]]
* 1 tsp [[cookbook:salt|salt]]
* 1½ cups (360 ml) [[cookbook:buttermilk|buttermilk]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[cookbook:butter|butter]], cut into [[Cookbook:Pea|pea]]-sized cubes

==Procedure==
# Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (180°C)
# Combine dry ingredients. Rub in butter until crumbly.
# Mix in buttermilk to make a soft, workable [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]]. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] dough briefly.
# Make dough into a disc about 3 inches thick. Cut an X shape in dough with a knife (1 cm or so deep). Transfer to an oiled or [[Cookbook:Parchment Paper|parchment]]-lined [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|baking sheet]].
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] at 350°F (180°C) for 50–70 minutes (depending on your oven) until a [[Cookbook:Skewer|skewer]] stuck in comes out with no "gooeyness" on it
# Let cool 5–10 minutes after taking from the oven, then break apart with your hands into serving-sized chunks.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Optionally mix in [[Cookbook:Blueberry|blueberries]], [[Cookbook:Raisin|raisins]], or [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] to taste.
